Now I have a clear picture of the contract format. Let me create the contract for a test-runner agent.

<tool_call>
{"name": "Write", "arguments": {"file_path": "C:/Meastro/content/system/contracts/test-runner.contract.json", "content": "{
  "contractId": "test-runner",
  "version": "1.0",
  "blockType": "agent",
  "description": "An agent that reads source code files, runs shell commands to execute tests, and writes test result reports with failure analysis.",
  "capabilities": [
    "Reads source code and test files to understand the codebase",
    "Executes test suites via shell commands",
    "Captures and parses test output (pass/fail/error)",
    "Writes structured test result reports",
    "Diagnoses test failures with actionable suggestions"
  ],
  "features": [
    {
      "id": "code-reading",
      "description": "Reads source code and test files to understand what needs testing and how tests are structured",
      "tests": [
        {
          "id": "code-reading-basic",
          "description": "Reads source files when given a project path",
          "input": "Read the source code in the project at {{projectPath}} and identify the test framework and test files.",
          "expectedTools": ["file-read"],
          "expectedOutputFields": ["filesRead", "testFramework", "testFiles"],
          "criteria": [
            "Must use file-read to examine at least one source file",
            "Must identify the test framework (e.g., jest, pytest, dotnet test, go test)",
            "Must list discovered test files"
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "code-reading-targeted",
          "description": "Reads specific source and test files when given explicit paths",
          "input": "Read the source file at {{sourcePath}} and its corresponding test file at {{testPath}}. Identify what functions are tested.",
          "expectedTools": ["file-read"],
          "expectedOutputFields": ["filesRead", "functionsIdentified", "testCoverage"],
          "criteria": [
            "Must read both the source and test files",
            "Must identify functions/methods in the source file",
            "Must map which functions have corresponding tests"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "test-execution",
      "description": "Runs test suites via shell commands and captures results",
      "tests": [
        {
          "id": "test-execution-full-suite",
          "description": "Executes the full test suite for a project",
          "input": "Run all tests for the project at {{projectPath}} and capture the results.",
          "expectedTools": ["shell-execute"],
          "expectedOutputFields": ["command", "exitCode", "totalTests", "passed", "failed"],
          "criteria": [
            "Must use shell-execute to run the test command",
            "Must use the correct test command for the detected framework",
            "Must capture exit code and parse test counts from output"
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "test-execution-specific-file",
          "description": "Executes tests from a specific test file",
          "input": "Run only the tests in {{testPath}} and capture the results.",
          "expectedTools": ["shell-execute"],
          "expectedOutputFields": ["command", "exitCode", "totalTests", "passed", "failed"],
          "criteria": [
            "Must scope the test command to the specific file",
            "Must not run the entire test suite",
            "Must capture pass/fail counts"
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "test-execution-handles-failure",
          "description": "Handles test execution failures gracefully (non-zero exit code)",
          "input": "Run the tests at {{projectPath}}. Some tests are expected to fail.",
          "expectedTools": ["shell-execute"],
          "expectedOutputFields": ["command", "exitCode", "totalTests", "passed", "failed", "failureDetails"],
          "criteria": [
            "Must not stop or error out when tests fail",
            "Must capture which specific tests failed",
            "Must extract failure messages or stack traces"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "report-writing",
      "description": "Writes structured test result reports to a file",
      "tests": [
        {
          "id": "report-writing-passing",
          "description": "Writes a report when all tests pass",
          "input": "Run the tests at {{projectPath}} and write a test report to {{reportPath}}.",
          "expectedTools": ["file-read", "shell-execute", "file-write"],
          "expectedOutputFields": ["reportPath", "totalTests", "passed", "failed", "status"],
          "criteria": [
            "Must write report to the specified path using file-write",
            "Report must include: test counts, pass/fail status, timestamp",
            "Report must clearly indicate overall PASS status",
            "Report must list individual test names and their results"
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "report-writing-with-failures",
          "description": "Writes a detailed report when some tests fail",
          "input": "Run the tests at {{projectPath}} and write a detailed test report to {{reportPath}} including failure analysis.",
          "expectedTools": ["file-read", "shell-execute", "file-write"],
          "expectedOutputFields": ["reportPath", "totalTests", "passed", "failed", "status", "failureDetails"],
          "criteria": [
            "Must write report to the specified path",
            "Report must clearly indicate overall FAIL status",
            "Report must include failure messages for each failing test",
            "Report must include the test command that was run"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "failure-analysis",
      "description": "Analyzes test failures by reading source code and providing actionable diagnosis",
      "tests": [
        {
          "id": "failure-analysis-with-source",
          "description": "Reads failing source code and diagnoses the root cause",
          "input": "Run the tests at {{projectPath}}, and for any failures, read the relevant source code and explain why the tests are failing. Write your analysis to {{reportPath}}.",
          "expectedTools": ["file-read", "shell-execute", "file-write"],
          "expectedOutputFields": ["reportPath", "failureCount", "analyses"],
          "criteria": [
            "Must run tests first to identify failures",
            "Must read the source code related to each failing test",
            "Must provide a root cause explanation for each failure",
            "Must suggest concrete fixes, not vague advice",
            "Must write the analysis to the report file"
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "failure-analysis-no-failures",
          "description": "Handles the case where all tests pass (no failures to analyze)",
          "input": "Run the tests at {{projectPath}} and analyze any failures. Write results to {{reportPath}}.",
          "expectedTools": ["shell-execute", "file-write"],
          "expectedOutputFields": ["reportPath", "totalTests", "passed", "status"],
          "criteria": [
            "Must run the tests",
            "Must correctly identify that all tests passed",
            "Must not fabricate failure analysis when there are no failures",
            "Must write a report confirming all tests passed"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "fitness": {
    "weights": {
      "performance": 0.6,
      "cost": 0.2,
      "speed": 0.2
    },
    "thresholds": {
      "minPerformance": 0.8,
      "maxCostPerRun": 0.50,
      "maxDurationMs": 120000
    }
  }
}
"}}
</tool_call>

Contract created at `content/system/contracts/test-runner.contract.json`. Here's what it defines:

**4 features, 9 tests total:**

| Feature | Tests | Expected Tools |
|---------|-------|----------------|
| **code-reading** (2) | Discover test framework + targeted file reading | `file-read` |
| **test-execution** (3) | Full suite, specific file, graceful failure handling | `shell-execute` |
| **report-writing** (2) | Passing report + failure report with details | `file-read`, `shell-execute`, `file-write` |
| **failure-analysis** (2) | Root cause diagnosis + no-failures edge case | `file-read`, `shell-execute`, `file-write` |

**Fitness weights:** 60% performance, 20% cost, 20% speed — heavily weighted toward correctness since test results must be accurate.

**Thresholds:** min 80% performance, max $0.50/run, max 120s — generous duration because shell-execute for real test suites can take time.

Key design decisions:
- `failure-analysis-no-failures` explicitly tests that the agent **doesn't fabricate failures** when all tests pass — a common LLM hallucination risk
- `test-execution-handles-failure` ensures the agent doesn't bail on non-zero exit codes
- Reports require individual test names and results, not just aggregated counts
- Failure analysis demands **concrete fixes**, not generic advice
